transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve failed my family and that everything that’s gone wrong is my fault. My wife and my cousin insisted that I come in to talk to someone, so that's why I'm here today.
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt the exact opposite—such as being unusually happy, highly energetic, or needing very little sleep?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I have never had times where I felt unusually happy, highly energetic, or needed very little sleep, and my mood has never swung in that direction. It has really only been the opposite, especially lately.
Have you ever had periods in the past, lasting at least a few weeks, where you felt this same kind of deep depression or sadness, or is this the very first time you are experiencing this?

No, I’ve never felt this way before, and this is the very first time I am experiencing such deep sadness. Before the big fight with my daughter, I generally felt proud of my work and our family life. It’s all very new and heavy for me.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness and self-blame? Has it been happening nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I've been feeling this way for about eight months now, ever since my daughter moved away after our big fight. It is a constant, heavy feeling that I experience pretty much every single day, so it has been going on for much longer than just two weeks.
Along with this sadness, have you lost interest or pleasure in the activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, I really have. I used to get so excited about closing a sales deal or grilling for the whole family on Sundays, but now it all feels pointless and I just go through the motions. I even make excuses to skip family gatherings because I just can't find any enjoyment in them anymore.
Have you also been experiencing physical changes, such as trouble sleeping, constant fatigue, or changes in your appetite?

Yes, my sleep has been terrible—I lie awake for hours staring at the ceiling and then wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with my mind racing about my daughter and work. Even if I manage to get a little sleep, I feel completely worn out and exhausted when the alarm goes off. My appetite hasn't really changed, but these sleep issues are constant.
Have you noticed any new difficulties with concentrating, making decisions, or focusing on your daily tasks at work or home?
I haven't really noticed any specific issues with my concentration or making decisions. I'm not really sure if that has changed for me.
During this difficult time, have you had any thoughts of death, hurting yourself, or that life is no longer worth living?

It’s hard to admit, but I’ve been having those thoughts, like maybe my family would be better off financially and emotionally if I weren't around. Sometimes I think it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up, and I've even found myself picturing how I might do it when I'm driving alone on the highway.
